entries.title: The will
entries.text: Stay in Vale Manor and find "the Eighth Record" before midnight on the seventh day. That is the whole condition. Nobody will say what the Eighth Record is.

entries.title: Vale Manor
entries.text: Outside Bellweather, Oregon. Every generation added something to it. Nobody seems to have taken anything away.

entries.title: The Vales
entries.text: Either the Vales built Bellweather, or Bellweather was built around the Vales. The town can't seem to decide.

entries.title: What is the Eighth Record?
entries.text: A document? A book? A room? The will only names it.

entries.title: Why me?
entries.text: I had never heard of Arthur Vale before the letter from his lawyers.

entries.title: Arthur Vale
entries.text: The last owner of Vale Manor. Died this September. He left me the house, on a condition, and a letter that opens with an apology for failing.

entries.title: Hawthorne & Mercer
entries.text: Arthur's executors. Two old Bellweather names sharing one letterhead. "We are not permitted to assist you further." Permitted by whom?

entries.title: Who keeps this house?
entries.text: The front lock was freshly oiled. Arthur was dying for months. Someone has been looking after the place.

entries.title: Margaret Vale
entries.text: 1816–1891. Her portrait hangs in the entrance hall. She was painted with a pen in her hand, not a fan or a book.

entries.title: Elias Vale
entries.text: 1812–1880. The first Vale here. The portrait gives him a surveyor's chain and dirty hands.

entries.title: Bellweather
entries.text: In the 1880 painting: a mill, a rail spur, a church, and seven big houses along the ridge.

entries.title: The ticking
entries.text: The only clock in the hall is stopped. Something in the walls keeps time anyway.

entries.title: Arthur's study
entries.text: Boxes labelled with family names, all empty. A corkboard with nothing left on it but pinholes.

entries.title: The Bellweather Disappearance
entries.text: 17 November 1936. Eleven people at dinner in this house. By morning, none of them. Four were Vales.

entries.title: Why 2:17?
entries.text: The clock stopped at 2:17. Arthur wrote it down as if it were an instruction.

entries.title: "Room measurements don't match"
entries.text: A policeman's pencil, in 1936: the rooms don't fit inside the walls. Which rooms?

entries.title: Two versions of one night
entries.text:
The police report: the west wing door was bolted from the inside, the clock stopped in the west library.
The newspaper: every door unlocked, the clock in the dining hall, a power failure.
A power failure doesn't stop a wind-up clock.

entries.title: Edmund Vale
entries.text: Arthur's father. One of the eleven. Arthur was seven, at school in Portland.

entries.title: The Meridian Society
entries.text: October 1936, a month before the disappearance: seven chairs for seven families. One chair has been cut out of the print.

entries.title: "One refused"
entries.text: "Seven remained. One refused." Seven of what? Refused what?

entries.title: Dr. Julian Whitmore
entries.text: Arthur's pencil on the back of the photograph: "Julian W.? — the eighth?" Arthur also told me not to trust him.

entries.title: Too many marks
entries.text: In the photograph, the marks on the floor don't match the number of chairs.

entries.title: Knocking
entries.text: Three knocks inside the study's north wall. I didn't answer.

entries.title: Circle, line, seven points
entries.text: Stamped on the brass study key. It looks like a seal. Whose?

entries.title: The west library
entries.text: Where the police found the clock stopped. The bulbs have been taken out of every fitting.

entries.title: Behind the shelves
entries.text: Between the library and the study, a wall 1.2 metres thicker than any plan would show. Inside it, a passage running west, and down.

entries.title: Circle, line, eight points
entries.text: The same seal, with eight points. Cut into stone the house was built around.

entries.title: Survey leaf, 1791
entries.text: French, half a century before the Vales came. "Huit points. Huit témoins." Eight points. Eight witnesses. And: the register was already there.
